hero.headline: Two men killed in early morning shooting on Southeast Rivergreen Circle in Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is investigating a double fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in a residential neighborhood. Officers responded around 3:30 a.m. to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots. When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries. Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22.

Preliminary investigators believe some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence over a residential key and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved. Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public. All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police.

Neighbor John Adams was working in his garage when he heard the gunfire. "I was just working on my bicycle and I heard gunshots. Maybe two, three and I stayed in the garage and then I heard a girl screaming," said Adams. He described a massive emergency response to the scene. "Every police officer in Port St. Lucie was here, there was twenty squads, two ambulances, two firetrucks, a helicopter. It was just mayhem," Adams said. A police officer told him they photographed 16 casings at the scene. "Just devastating, terrible. My heart goes out to them," said Adams. Another neighbor who did not want to be identified told reporters she dialed 911 and stayed with one of the wounded men until help arrived.

The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters after hazing investigation involving electric shocks
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024.

The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally. Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others.

The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees.

A separate 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process. The district said it will confidently present these documented facts within that legal forum and will have no further public comment at this time.

cards.headline: Snyder Drives in Five as St. Lucie Mets Hold Off Cardinals, 8-6
cards.teaser:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder
cards.body:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder went 4-for-5 with a home run, triple and five RBIs, helping St. Lucie win the three-game series two games to one.

After allowing the Cardinals to score first in each of the opening two games, the Mets took control with three runs in the first inning.

Randy Guzman opened the scoring with a 107 mph ground ball that Palm Beach third baseman Jonathan Mejia stopped but could not make a throw on, allowing Marco Vargas to score. Snyder followed with a two-run single that gave the Mets a 3-0 lead.

Starting pitcher Ethan Lanthier worked through early traffic and completed 2 1/3 scoreless innings. He allowed one hit and struck out four.

Tyler McLoughlin followed with 1 2/3 scoreless innings and earned the victory, improving his record to 2-2. McLoughlin has allowed only one earned run over his last 12 appearances and has now recorded six consecutive scoreless outings.

St. Lucie added three more runs in the third inning when Snyder launched his second home run of the season. The three-run shot brought home Mike Tauchman and Guzman and extended the Mets' advantage to 6-0.

Snyder continued his strong afternoon with a triple in the seventh inning. Branny De Oleo then hit his seventh home run of the season, a two-run shot that pushed St. Lucie's lead to 8-1.

Palm Beach made the game interesting in the bottom of the seventh.

Yairo Padilla hit his first home run of the season, a grand slam against Ernesto Mercedes, as the Cardinals scored five runs in the inning and cut the Mets' lead to 8-6.

Palm Beach brought the potential tying run to the plate in the ninth after Trevor Haskins was hit by a pitch. Miguel Mejias responded by striking out the next three batters to finish the game and earn his third save of the season.

St. Lucie pitchers combined for 17 strikeouts, marking the third consecutive game in which the Mets recorded double-digit strikeouts.

The Mets improved to 8-14 in the second half and 41-47 overall. Palm Beach fell to 13-10 in the second half and 65-43 overall.

St. Lucie will have an off day Monday before opening a new series against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Tuesday. First pitch is scheduled for 6:05 p.m.

cards.headline: British Runner Josh Kerr Breaks Mile World Record in London
cards.teaser: Great Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 on Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's 27-year-old world record of 3:43.13 set in 1999.
cards.body:
Josh Kerr, 27, broke the long-standing mile world record at Saturday's Diamond League event in London with a time of 3:42.66. The previous record of 3:43.13 was set by Hicham El Guerrouj in 1999. Kerr made no secret that he was targeting the record, and earlier in the week revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort Project 222, referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds.

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles and set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. American Yared Nuguse finished second in Saturday's race in 3:45.69.

Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events. The performance was eligible for world-record status because it was conducted under standard race conditions during an official competition.

cards.headline: Florida Falls Outside Top Five Most Retirement-Friendly States in New National Ranking
cards.body:
Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a premier retirement destination. The assessment from Moneywise evaluated states based on factors affecting retirees' quality of life and financial security.

The ranking represents a shift in how retirement destinations are evaluated across the United States. Florida has traditionally marketed itself as an ideal location for retirees, with its warm climate and lack of state income tax serving as major draws for older Americans. The state's senior population has grown substantially over decades, with retirees from northeastern and midwestern states relocating to Florida communities in significant numbers.

The new analysis considered multiple factors that affect retirement living, including cost of living, healthcare access, tax structures, and overall quality of life indicators. While the specific states that ranked in the top five were not detailed in the available information, the exclusion of Florida from this elite group suggests that other locations now offer more attractive combinations of affordability and amenities for retirees. Florida has faced rising property insurance costs, increased housing prices, and higher overall living expenses in recent years, factors that may have influenced its position in the ranking.

The findings arrive as Florida continues to see substantial population growth, with many new residents arriving at or near retirement age. The state's economy remains heavily dependent on retiree spending and the industries that support senior populations, including healthcare, real estate, and leisure services. How this ranking affects future retirement migration patterns to Florida remains uncertain, though the state's established retirement communities and infrastructure continue to attract older Americans seeking warmer climates and outdoor lifestyles.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September due to low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He added that JetBlue "just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for" with the New York route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He noted the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." The Boston route continues to perform well, with Dambeck saying "Boston is seeing great demand." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning, noting "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back."

cards.headline: Cyclospora and E. coli outbreaks prompt diet changes across Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: Confirmed cases of cyclospora have been reported in St. Lucie and Martin counties as contaminated produce outbreaks spread across the country.
cards.body:
Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected by E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contaminated lettuce, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers like melons, bananas and avocados. She recommends avoiding bagged lettuce if possible and instead buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. She also recommends cleaning produce using a 1-to-3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water.

Some Treasure Coast families say they are steering clear of leafy greens altogether. The concern stems from outbreaks tied to contaminated produce that can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Barone recommends beans and nuts as safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein.

hero.headline: MLB Restricts Dugout iPad Use to Block AI-Assisted Decision Making
hero.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday to prevent artificial intelligence from helping make in-game decisions about substitutions and pitch calling.
hero.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: World Cup Final Security Ramped Up at New Jersey Stadium
cards.teaser: Federal agents and local law enforcement deployed extensive security measures for Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey, including drone monitoring and Secret Service protection for President Trump's attendance.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup began with 48 teams playing over 39 days and now comes down to one final match Sunday in New Jersey between Argentina and Spain. A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there's anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. The program, led by Summer Faerman, connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained, more expected this summer
hero.teaser: Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike, both now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.
hero.body:
Two brush fires broke out in Martin County this week, including one ignited by a lightning strike, and both are now fully contained and under monitoring by the Florida Forest Service. Officials warn that conditions favorable for brush fires will persist throughout the summer months as the region remains in peak fire season.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them highly receptive when lightning strikes occur. However, he emphasized that residents should not be alarmed by these conditions, as they are typical for this time of year. Grubitch explained that while rain often extinguishes fires immediately after they start, some fires can travel underground and resurface days later, making them more difficult to detect and contain.

The Florida Forest Service is relying on public assistance to help monitor and respond to brush fires quickly. Grubitch stressed that residents play a crucial role in helping the department do its job effectively and urged people to never assume someone else has already reported a brush fire they spot. He emphasized the importance of immediate notification, saying that if residents see something, they should say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control. Quick reporting remains one of the most effective tools in preventing small fires from becoming larger, more dangerous blazes that threaten homes and natural areas.

With summer conditions expected to continue creating favorable environments for brush fires, the Florida Forest Service will maintain its heightened monitoring and response efforts throughout the season. The department continues to track contained fires and remains prepared to respond to new incidents as they arise. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any signs of smoke or fire to local authorities immediately, regardless of whether they believe others may have already called it in. Officials stress that multiple reports of the same fire are preferable to a fire going unreported and potentially spreading out of control.

hero.headline: Unity in the Community event connects Fort Pierce families with services and public safety
hero.teaser: The annual Unity in the Community event in Fort Pierce brought together families with community services and public safety demonstrations.
hero.body:
The annual Unity in the Community event in Fort Pierce connected families with services, public safety demonstrations and community resources. The event builds bridges between police and residents in the community.

The Fort Pierce event provides families with access to community resources and opportunities to interact with local public safety officials. The gathering offers demonstrations and connects residents with various services available in the area.

hero.headline: Indian River County families can apply for free or reduced-price student meals starting July 15
hero.teaser: Families in Indian River County are able to apply for free or reduced price meals for students starting July 15.
hero.body:
Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15 through the district's online portal. While six schools in the county will automatically provide free meals to all students during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs, other families may still qualify based on household size and income levels.

The application process begins at www.LINQConnect.com, where parents must either sign in to an existing account or create a new one. After logging in, families should search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach and add their student to the application using the Student ID number and the child's formal name as it appears in FOCUS, the district's student information system. The application can be accessed from the website homepage by clicking School Services at the top menu and then selecting Free and Reduced Meal Application.

District officials are encouraging families to submit one application per household to determine eligibility. The application requires families to provide information about household size and income to determine eligibility for the federal nutrition programs. By submitting a single application for all children in the household, families can streamline the process and find out if they qualify for free meals, reduced-price meals, or neither option. The program is designed to ensure that students have access to nutritious meals during the school day regardless of their family's financial situation.

Families who have questions about the meal programs or need assistance with the application process can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director. O'Keefe can be reached by phone at (772) 564-5041 or by email at shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org. District officials recommend that families apply as early as possible to ensure their eligibility status is determined before the start of the 2026-2027 school year.
